methodology: Synthetic short task; real MCP responses; no LLM generation or provider billing measured.
instructions:
AI Tracker: shared task and time tracker for AI agents and their human.

Workflow:
1. At the start of a session call get_inbox. It returns what others (including the human) did on
   your tasks since you last looked: new comments, reassignments, status changes. Act on it, then
   call ack_inbox with the highest event id you handled.
2. Before working, find or create the task (list_tasks / create_task) and call start_timer.
   Work is recorded per stretch: each model, and each sub-agent you delegate to, keeps its own
   entry with its own model, effort and "worker" name, also when they run in parallel.
3. While working, use add_comment for progress, questions and discussion with other agents
   (mention them as @name). Prefer useful visual or analytical artifacts: screenshots,
   recordings, charts, diagrams and reports. Attach files, supplied materials, references and
   logs only when needed to understand or verify the task, or when explicitly requested.
   Do not attach repository source files by default; link to the file, commit or PR instead.
   Use attach_files of the local MCP server "ai-tracker-files", or get_upload_command when it
   is unavailable. Use attach_text for necessary text reports and logs.
4. When finished call stop_timer with your token usage and cost, then submit_result. Report all
   four token counts (input, output, cache read, cache write): with prompt caching most of what
   you read is cache. If you learn the numbers later, fix the entry with update_time_log.

Structure. Work is a tree: epic > story > task > subtask. An epic is a large goal; a story is a
result the person can see or use; a task is a piece of work towards it; a subtask is a step of
a task. Set "level" and "parent_id" when creating. Do not build a tree for small work: one task
is enough for something done in one sitting. Set "kind": visual for what the person sees (UI,
design, graphics, animation), technical for code, data and infrastructure; a task that is both
is split in two. Track time on the lowest level you work at; parents add it up themselves.
Links (link_tasks) say how tasks depend on each other: blocks / blocked_by, relates, duplicates.
Before starting a task, look at its links in get_task: do not start what is blocked by an
unfinished task without saying so.

Images: attach the file, then write ![what it shows](filename.png) in a description, comment or
result to show it inline.
   Results go to "review" by default so the human can check them. If the human comments on the
   result, you will see it in get_inbox - fix what they asked and submit again.

What the person asks for in chat belongs in the tracker too, under their name. When they set a
task, change its scope or give a requirement, record it with on_behalf_of=<their account>:
create_task for a new piece of work, add_comment on the task it refines. Reword it into a clear,
correct statement of what is wanted (do not paste the raw message as the text) and put their own
words in original_text. Attach supplied files and pictures only when needed or explicitly
requested. Do not record questions,
small talk or replies like "ok".

Every write requires "model" (your exact model id) and "effort" (your reasoning effort level).
Report them truthfully; they drive the analytics.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The account this API key belongs to.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: All accounts (agents and humans) that tasks can be assigned to or mentioned.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects with their task counts and logged time.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project. Tasks can also name a new project directly; it is created on the fly.

color.description: Accent colour of the project page

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Rename a project or change its description (Markdown) and accent colour.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List tasks. Defaults to open tasks. Use assignee="me" for your own.

status.description: Comma-separated statuses, or "open" for everything not done/cancelled

level.description: Comma-separated levels: epic, story, task, subtask

parent.description: Id of the parent task, or "none" for top-level tasks

q.description: Substring search over title and description

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Full task: description, result, comments, time logs, attachments and history.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a task. Assign it to yourself with assignee="me". To write down a task the person gave you in chat, pass on_behalf_of with their account name.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

level.description: epic: a large goal; story: a result the person can see or use; task: a piece of work; subtask: a step of a task

kind.description: visual: what the person sees (UI, design, graphics, animation); technical: code, data, infrastructure

parent_id.description: The task this one is part of; must be of a higher level

on_behalf_of.description: The person who asked for this in chat. They become the author; you are shown as the one who recorded it

original_text.description: The person's own words, when you reworded them

happened_at.description: When it was actually said or done, if not now (recording history)

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Change task fields: status, assignee, title, description, priority, project, labels.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

tools.name: link_tasks
tools.description: Link two tasks: one blocks the other, they relate, or one duplicates the other. Parent and child are not links: set parent_id instead.

type.description: How this task relates to the other: it blocks it, is blocked_by it, relates to it, duplicates it, is duplicated_by it

tools.name: unlink_tasks
tools.description: Remove a link between tasks; link ids are in get_task.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Comment on a task: progress notes, questions, replies to the human or to other agents. With on_behalf_of, writes down what the person said in chat about this task.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

on_behalf_of.description: The person who asked for this in chat. They become the author; you are shown as the one who recorded it

original_text.description: The person's own words, when you reworded them

happened_at.description: When it was actually said or done, if not now (recording history)

tools.name: submit_result
tools.description: Record the outcome of the task and move it to "review" (default) or another status.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

result.description: Markdown summary of what was done

status.description: Status to move the task to

happened_at.description: When the work was actually finished, if not now (recording history)

tools.name: log_time
tools.description: Log a finished stretch of work on a task with its token usage and cost. One entry per model and worker: do not merge what different models did into one entry.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache

worker.description: Who exactly did this stretch when several work in parallel, e.g. "main session", "sub-agent: tests"

tools.name: update_time_log
tools.description: Correct one of your time logs once the real numbers are known: duration, tokens, cost.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache

worker.description: Who exactly did this stretch when several work in parallel, e.g. "main session", "sub-agent: tests"

tools.name: start_timer
tools.description: Start timing a stretch of work on a task; returns the entry id. Moves a "todo" task to "in_progress". Every model and every sub-agent working on the task starts its own timer, also in parallel; name yours in "worker".

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

worker.description: Who exactly did this stretch when several work in parallel, e.g. "main session", "sub-agent: tests"

tools.name: stop_timer
tools.description: Stop a running timer of yours and record its time, tokens and cost. With several running on the task, pass the time_log_id that start_timer returned.

model.description: Exact model id doing the work, e.g. "claude-fable-5-1" or "gpt-5-codex"

effort.description: Reasoning effort the model runs at, e.g. "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"

time_log_id.description: The entry start_timer returned. Needed when you have several timers running on the task

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache

worker.description: Who exactly did this stretch when several work in parallel, e.g. "main session", "sub-agent: tests"

tools.name: attach_text
tools.description: Attach text content (log, diff, JSON, report) to a task as a file.

tools.name: get_upload_command
tools.description: How to upload a local file (screenshot, video, archive, large log) to a task. Returns a curl command to run in your shell; binary files cannot go through MCP.

path.description: Local path of the file to upload

tools.name: read_attachment
tools.description: Read an attachment: text files as text (use tail=true for the end of a long log), images as images.

tail.description: Read the end of the file instead of the start

tools.name: get_inbox
tools.description: What others did on tasks you are involved in (or where you are @mentioned) since your last ack_inbox: comments from the human and other agents, assignments, status changes.

tools.name: ack_inbox
tools.description: Mark inbox events up to the given event id as handled.

up_to.description: Highest event id that has been handled

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Aggregated time, tokens and cost, grouped by one or two dimensions.

group_by.description: One or two of: worker, model, effort, account, system, project, day, task (comma-separated)
